title: A following value token denotes a domain-specific measurement, not a universal ordinal
summary: GDT764 contains repeated X–daiin fields and leaves several axes open. The hypothesis is that a repeated value form is interpreted relative to a selected domain, while a universal ordinal would remain unchanged across X.

design.unit: source-bound complete records or visual-text contexts named in source_observation
design.prediction: changing X while holding the value token fixed should alter the independently observable value domain; a universal ordinal predicts the same domain across X
design.countermodel: Near IDEA000087/head-conditioned value axis; retained only as a narrower rival about domain shift, not a German axis label.
design.falsifier: The same X change leaves an independently observed domain invariant, or domain changes occur without X change.
design.principal_risk: No independent domain marker currently exists; GDT764 axes are working renderings.

evidence.quote:
This is materially more informative than rendering three unrelated labels.
H1 supplies the record/form scope; the immediate X whole bounds the kind of
field in which III occurs. One axis is selected strongly (`qoty`), one remains
a weak provisional choice (`oteody`), and three preserve an open axis while
still receiving a usable bounded rendering (`dal`, `qopchdy`, `ofchy`).

design.smallest_test: Audit the five existing triples for non-glossed neighboring value/quantity markers and predeclare one held contrast.
design.selection_status: raw_unreviewed; no readiness or novelty claim
